title: Security Trading Policy

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Persons having authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the Company's activities, directly or indirectly, including any Director (executive or otherwise); the Board determines who is KMP. Closed Periods, the short-term trading ban and the approval/notification regime apply uniformly to this tier.

tiers.name: Chairman
tiers.description: The Chairman; distinguished only for clearance, which is given by the Board rather than the Chairman.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Nominees, agents or other associates such as family members, family trusts and family companies, through whom dealings by Key Management Personnel are also caught.

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to release of the Company's Annual Financial Report
windows.end_anchor: 48 hours after release of the Company's Annual Financial Report

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to release of the Half Year Financial Report
windows.end_anchor: 48 hours after release of the Half Year Financial Report

windows.end_anchor: 48 hours after release of the Company's quarterly reports (if applicable)

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may at its discretion vary a Closed Period by general announcement to all Key Management Personnel before or during that Closed Period; regardless of any variation, a person possessing price sensitive information must not deal at any time. Confidentiality of any variation is not addressed.

rules.detail: The policy applies only to 'the sale and purchase of any securities of the Company and its subsidiaries on issue from time to time'; it never mentions derivatives, options over securities issued by third parties, or any instrument other than the Company's own securities and its employee scheme options.
Hedging is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
Monetisation structures such as prepaid forwards are not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
Short selling is not named; the only trading-style restriction is the short-term trading ban in 4.2, which addresses holding period rather than short sales.
Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere in the policy.
CFDs and other third-party derivative products are not mentioned; the policy's scope is limited to buying, selling or exercising rights in the Company's own securities.

Margin lending is expressly contemplated and not restricted: the policy addresses the consequences of a margin loan (an exempt forced-sale disposal, and no insider trading breach for a default sale) without imposing any approval requirement on entering the loan itself, which falls outside the policy's 'buy, sell or exercise rights' scope.
rules.evidence: Where Company securities are provided to a lender as security by way of mortgage or charge, a sale that occurs under that mortgage or charge as a consequence of default would not breach insider trading laws.

rules.detail: Granting security over Company securities by way of mortgage or charge to a lender is expressly contemplated and not itself restricted or made subject to approval; only the resulting disposal on default is addressed (and is exempted from insider trading liability).
rules.evidence: Where Company securities are provided to a lender as security by way of mortgage or charge, a sale that occurs under that mortgage or charge as a consequence of default would not breach insider trading laws.

rules.detail: Any secured financing arrangement over Company securities (margin lending, mortgage or charge) is contemplated by the policy and not itself prohibited or subject to prior approval; only the forced-sale consequence is addressed.
rules.evidence: dispose of securities of the Company resulting from a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement

rules.detail: Blanket ban on short-term trading with no defined holding period, except for the exercise of options followed by a prompt sale of the resulting shares.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel should never engage in short-term trading of the Company's securities except for the exercise of options where the shares will be sold shortly thereafter.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: within 2 business days of the transaction occurring
clearance.evidence: Any Key Management Personnel (other than the Chairman) wishing to buy, sell or exercise rights in relation to the Company's securities must obtain the prior written approval of the Chairman or the Board before doing so.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: within 2 business days of the transaction occurring
clearance.evidence: If the Chairman wishes to buy, sell or exercise rights in relation to the Company's securities, the Chairman must obtain the prior approval of the Board before doing so.

carve_outs: exercise of options where the shares will be sold shortly thereafter
short_term.evidence: Key Management Personnel should never engage in short-term trading of the Company's securities except for the exercise of options where the shares will be sold shortly thereafter.

exceptions.evidence: acquire ordinary shares in the Company by conversion of securities giving a right of conversion to ordinary shares;
acquire Company securities under a bonus issue made to all holders of securities of the same class;
acquire Company securities under a dividend reinvestment, or top-up plan that is available to all holders or securities of the same class;
acquire, or agree to acquire or exercise options under an employee incentive scheme (as that term is defined in the ASX Listing Rules);

withdraw ordinary shares in the Company held on behalf of the Key Management Personnel in an employee incentive scheme (as that term is defined in the ASX Listing Rules) where the withdrawal is permitted by the rules of that scheme;
acquire ordinary shares in the Company as a result of the exercise of options held under an employee option scheme;
transfer securities of the Company already held into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the restricted person is a beneficiary;

make an investment in, or trade in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in the securities of the Company) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party;

where a restricted person is a trustee, trade in the securities of the Company by that trust, provided the restricted person is not a beneficiary of the trust and any decision to trade during a prohibited period is taken by the other trustees or by the investment managers independently of the restricted person;
undertake to accept, or accept, a takeover offer;

trade under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders, such as a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back, where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Board.
dispose of securities of the Company resulting from a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement;

exercise (but not sell securities following exercise) an option or a right under an employee incentive scheme, or convert a convertible security, where the final date for the exercise of the option or right, or the conversion of the security, falls during a prohibited period
trade under a non-discretionary trading plan for which prior written clearance has been provided in accordance with procedures set out in this Policy.

exceptions.approver: the Board (or, where the applicant is a Board member, all other members of the Board)
exceptions.evidence: Key Management Personnel who are not in possession of inside information in relation to the Company, may be given prior written clearance by the Board to sell or otherwise dispose of Company securities in a Closed Period where the person is in severe financial hardship or where there are exceptional circumstances as set out in this policy.

Exceptional circumstances may apply to the disposal of Company securities by a Key Management Personnel if the person is required by a court order, a court enforceable undertaking for example in a bona fide family settlement, to transfer or sell securities of the Company, or there is some other overriding legal or regulatory requirement to do so.

financing_disclosure: Key Management Personnel (all): trigger = disposal of Company securities resulting from a secured lender (e.g. margin lender, mortgagee or chargee) exercising its rights; to the Company Secretary in writing; within 2 business days of the transaction occurring, under the general post-trade notification duty.

exemption_authority: The Board (or, if the applicant is a Board member, all other Board members) may give prior written clearance for a Key Management Personnel to sell or otherwise dispose of Company securities during a Closed Period on grounds of severe financial hardship (a pressing financial commitment satisfiable only by selling) or exceptional circumstances (a court order, court-enforceable undertaking, or other overriding legal or regulatory requirement). Any such exemption must be in writing and specify the time period during which the sale can be made; a hardship application requires supporting documentation and may need independent verification from the person's bank or accountant.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Where Company securities are provided to a lender as security by way of mortgage or charge, a sale that occurs under that mortgage or charge as a consequence of default would not breach insider trading laws.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike most peer policies, AZY expressly authorises a secured lender's enforcement sale even while the executive holds inside information, and separately lists such a disposal as something KMP 'may at any time' do, including during a Closed Period - materially de-risking a bank's ability to enforce its security over the collared shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This policy applies to both the sale and purchase of any securities of the Company and its subsidiaries on issue from time to time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The clearance and notification regime is built around buying, selling or exercising rights in the Company's own securities; entering an OTC put/call with a bank, or granting a mortgage/charge, may fall outside that regime altogether, though general insider trading law still applies independently of the policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the management of the sale of any significant volume of Company securities (ie a volume that would represent a volume in excess of 10% of the total securities held by the seller prior to the sale, or a volume to be sold that would be in excess of 10% of the average daily traded volume of the shares of the Company on the ASX for the preceding 20 trading days) by a Key Management Personnel needs to be discussed with the Board and the Company's legal advisers prior to the execution of any sale.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar-driven sale (e.g. on call exercise or unwind) exceeding either 10% threshold triggers a mandatory Board and legal-adviser discussion and a retained file note before execution.

bespoke_clauses.clause: it is not permissible to provide the exercise price of options by selling the shares acquired on the exercise of these options unless the sale of those shares occurs outside the periods specified in paragraph 4.1.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If the collared shares originate from option exercise, a sell-to-cover exercise cannot be used to fund the exercise price inside a Closed Period.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any exemption, if issued, will be in writing and shall contain a specified time period during which the sale of securities can be made.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar unwind cleared under the hardship or exceptional-circumstances route during a Closed Period is time-boxed by the Board's written exemption, so execution must occur within that specified window.

summary: A funded collar appears more workable here than under most peer policies because the financing leg is expressly contemplated: Key Management Personnel may provide Company securities to a lender as security by mortgage or charge, and a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising its rights (e.g. under a margin lending arrangement) is treated as an exception available 'at any time' - including in a Closed Period or while holding inside information - and expressly does not breach insider trading laws. The policy's clearance regime (prior written approval from the Chairman or Board, notification to the Company Secretary within 2 business days) is drafted narrowly around buying, selling or exercising rights in the Company's own securities, so it is unclear whether the OTC put/call themselves, or the grant of a mortgage/charge, are caught as a 'dealing' requiring approval at all; general insider trading law nonetheless still applies. Outside financing, ordinary dealing is barred during the two-week pre-results/48-hour post-results Closed Periods (subject to a written Board hardship or exceptional-circumstances exemption specifying a fixed sale window) and short-term trading is banned except for prompt sale on option exercise. A sale exceeding 10% of the individual's holding or 10% of 20-day average trading volume additionally requires prior Board and legal-adviser discussion and a file note. Overall: the loan leg is unusually well-protected, but Chairman/Board clearance should still be sought out of caution for the derivative legs, executed outside Closed Periods.
